newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - Australian contract miners.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RESEARCH ALERT - Australian contract miners.

text.p: The Australian contract mining industry has been in cyclical upturn for the last three years and evidence suggests the outlook remains positive for at least the next year, according to Adelaide-based broker Todd Partners.
"The industry is buoyant and there is no sign of a downturn," analyst Greg Cathro said in a sector research report.
However, investors should review the outlook periodically and take into account any plans individual companies had to resist a future industry downturn, he said.
The industry was characterised by a number of small to mid-size companies, both public and private, he said.
There is no one dominant or large company, Cathro said.
"Rationalisation amongst the listed participants is possible, although the needle for such reform may need to wait until industry conditions deteriorate," he said.

He said the listed companies with significant contract mining activities were: Ausdrill Ltd, Brandrill Ltd, Century Drilling Ltd, Eltin Ltd, Grimwood Davies Ltd, Henry Walker Group Ltd, Macmahon Holdings Ltd and Stanley Mining Services Ltd.
"Our recommendations for the coming year are Ausdrill, Brandrill and Century Drilling," the report said.
"Grimwood Davies compares well on an estimated earnings basis, but its margins seem above the average and subject to tightening."
"Stanley Mining also has appeal, with the only drawback being a low level of 1996 cashflow which hopefully will be corrected in 1997," it said.
"Henry Walker retains the best quality status for portfolio investors, and commands a market premium for that quality."

Cathro said investment in the growing industry may be an alternative to the more volatile mining companies, with contract miners offering consistent and relatively high dividend returns, attractive earnings fundamentals, and more predictable results.
"In the longer term the contract miners are not immune from the cyclical nature of the resources industry but in the shorter term they offer relative stability," he said.
Cathro said the resilience of each company when industry conditions did deteriorate was dependent upon a number of factors and individual characteristics.

"The drill and blast companies tend to have contracts of shorter duration. Some companies service the exploration side of mining as opposed to the production side. Some companies have diversified overseas or into different commodities," he said.

Cathro said the drill and blast companies, with their shorter term contracts and for whom value of contracts on hand was not suitable as an indicator of current year workloads, could be regarded as more volatile investments than complete service contractors.

The industry was capital intensive with high fixed costs, but increases in equity capital of the contract miners in general had been justified as the adjusted earnings per share figures and listed share prices had performed well, he said.
